quickAnswers.question: When can I check in for my United flight?
quickAnswers.answer: Check-in opens 24 hours before scheduled departure on united.com or the United app. Arrive early on travel day for bag drop and security.

quickAnswers.question: Can I choose my seat on United?
quickAnswers.answer: Yes — pick a seat when you book or later in Manage reservation. Seat choice and fees depend on your fare.

quickAnswers.question: How many bags can I bring?
quickAnswers.answer: Every traveler may bring a personal item. Carry-on and checked bag allowances and fees depend on fare, route and MileagePlus status.

learning.title: How do I check in for my flight?
learning.subtitle: Online and app check-in opens 24 hours before departure.
learning.summary: Check in on united.com or the United app starting 24 hours before your flight, then get your boarding pass and head to the airport.
learning.content:
How do I check in for my flight?

Check-in opens 24 hours before your scheduled departure.

What to do first
Open My trips on united.com or the United app, select your flight, and follow the check-in prompts for each traveler.

Boarding pass options
Save a mobile pass to your phone wallet, print at home, or use an airport kiosk or ticket counter.

When to escalate
If check-in is blocked or your name does not match your travel documents, contact United before you leave for the airport.

learning.title: Choose or change my seat
learning.subtitle: Pick a seat when booking or later in Manage reservation.
learning.summary: Choose your seat when booking or later in Manage reservation. Seat options and fees depend on your fare.
learning.content:
Choose or change my seat

You can pick a seat during booking or afterward.

What to do first
Open Manage reservation, select your trip, and choose Seats to pick available seats for each traveler.

Fare tip
Basic Economy, Economy, Economy Plus®, and premium cabins include different seat selection options and fees.

When to escalate
If you need accessible seating, contact Accessibility Services before your travel day.

learning.title: Baggage allowance and fees
learning.subtitle: Carry-on and checked bag rules for United travelers.
learning.summary: Allowances depend on your fare, route and MileagePlus status. Every traveler may bring a personal item.
learning.content:
Baggage allowance and fees

Know what you can bring before you pack.

What to do first
Review your trip confirmation for your carry-on and checked bag allowance, then use the baggage calculator for fees.

Special items
Sports equipment and oversized items may have extra rules or fees.

When to escalate
Report delayed or damaged bags at the airport baggage service office, then track the claim online.

learning.title: Change or cancel my flight
learning.subtitle: Changes, cancellations and future flight credits.
learning.summary: Most tickets can be changed or canceled online. Remaining value is often held as a future flight credit based on your fare.
learning.content:
Change or cancel my flight

Use Manage reservation to update your trip.

What to do first
Find your confirmation, then choose Change or Cancel and follow the fare rules shown for each traveler.

Same-day options
Same-day changes and standby may be available depending on fare and seat availability.

When to escalate
If United canceled your flight, review rebooking and refund options under Delays & cancellations.

learning.title: MileagePlus miles and Premier status
learning.subtitle: Earn miles, track Premier status and redeem awards.
learning.summary: MileagePlus members earn miles on flights and with partners. Premier status has annual qualifying thresholds.
learning.content:
MileagePlus miles and Premier status

Manage your loyalty benefits in your MileagePlus account.

What to do first
Sign in to view your miles balance and Premier progress.

Missing miles
Request credit for a past flight from your account activity if miles did not post.

When to escalate
For locked accounts or name changes, use the MileagePlus account update forms.

learning.title: What if my flight is delayed or canceled?
learning.subtitle: Rebooking, notifications and disruption help.
learning.summary: United will notify you of schedule changes. Rebook in the app or with an agent, and review voucher or refund options when eligible.
learning.content:
What if my flight is delayed or canceled?

Stay flexible when disruptions happen.

What to do first
Check your trip status in the app and accept a rebooked itinerary if offered.

Traveler options
Depending on the disruption, you may rebook, request a refund, or get additional help at the airport.

When to escalate
For overnight disruptions or expense reimbursement, use the Help Center request forms for vouchers or compensation.

learning.title: How do I use a future flight credit?
learning.subtitle: Apply unused value to a future United trip.
learning.summary: Future flight credits from eligible canceled trips can be applied at booking. Check expiration dates in your account.
learning.content:
How do I use a future flight credit?

Credits stay attached to the traveler named on the original ticket unless rules say otherwise.

What to do first
Sign in, open your travel credits, and note the amount and expiration before you book.

At checkout
Apply the credit on united.com or in the app when paying for a new trip.

When to escalate
If a credit is missing or expired early, contact United with your original confirmation number.

learning.title: Accessibility and special assistance
learning.subtitle: Wheelchair assistance, service animals and seating needs.
learning.summary: Request airport assistance and accessible seating ahead of travel so United can prepare for your trip.
learning.content:
Accessibility and special assistance

United can support a range of accessibility needs.

What to do first
Add assistance requests when you book or in Manage reservation before departure day.

Airport arrival
Allow extra time for assistance at check-in, security and boarding.

When to escalate
To discuss medical seating or service animal documentation, contact Accessibility Services before you fly.

learning.title: Pet Travel Policy - International Flights
learning.subtitle: Complete guide for traveling internationally with pets on United.
learning.summary: You can bring your pet on an international flight as long as it meets our weight and vaccination criteria. In-cabin and cargo travel have crate requirements, and you will need a valid health certificate issued within 10 days of departure.
learning.content:
Pet Travel Policy - International Flights

Effective January 1, 2025. Applies to all international flights.

Traveling internationally can be an exciting adventure, and for many pet owners, leaving their companions behind is out of the question. United offers an international pet travel policy designed to support a safe and comfortable journey.

Planning Ahead: Your First Steps
Contact the dedicated pet travel desk as soon as dates are confirmed. Availability is limited, destination requirements vary, and the pet reservation must be associated with the passenger booking.

In-Cabin Travel: Small Pets Welcome
Small dogs and cats may travel in an approved, ventilated, escape-proof carrier that fits under the seat. The animal must be able to stand and turn around naturally.

Checked Baggage: Larger Companions
Larger pets may travel in the climate-controlled cargo hold. Kennels must meet IATA requirements for size, construction, and ventilation.

Veterinary Health Certificate
Issued by a licensed veterinarian and completed within the destination's required travel window.

Rabies Vaccination Certificate
Proof of a current rabies vaccination is required for most international destinations.

Other Vaccinations
Additional vaccinations may be required by the destination country.

Import Permits
Some countries require an import permit obtained before travel.

Microchip
Most countries require an ISO-compliant identification microchip.

Policy reference
United pet travel specialists can explain destination requirements, but the pet owner is responsible for ensuring that all documentation is complete.

learning.title: Bring a Dog on International Flights
learning.subtitle: Complete guide for traveling internationally with your dog on United.
learning.summary: Dogs must be at least 8 weeks old, travel in an approved crate and have a current rabies vaccination. The pet fee is $125 each way in the cabin or $200 in the cargo hold.
learning.content:
Bring a Dog on International Flights

Effective January 1, 2025. Applies to all international flights with dogs.

Dogs must be at least 8 weeks old and fully weaned.

Approved hard-sided or soft-sided crate (41 in x 24 in x 28 in).

Maximum combined weight (dog + carrier) of 20 lbs for in-cabin travel.

Valid health certificate issued within 10 days of departure.

Current rabies vaccination required (administered at least 21 days before travel).

Additional vaccinations: Distemper, Parvovirus, and Bordetella.

Dog must remain in carrier throughout the flight.

Pet fee of $125 each way for in-cabin, $200 for cargo hold.

Country-specific requirements may apply.

Microchip identification recommended for international travel.

Policy reference
Pet Policy DOG-INT-2025

messages.content: How do I check in for my flight?

Check-in opens 24 hours before your scheduled departure.

1. Open My trips on united.com or in the United app.
2. Select your flight and follow the check-in prompts for each traveler.
3. Save a mobile boarding pass, print at home, or use an airport kiosk.

Arrive early on travel day for bag drop and security. If check-in is blocked or your name doesn’t match your travel documents, contact United before you leave for the airport.
citations: How do I check in for my flight?

messages.content:
Yes — you can usually change seats after booking.

1. Go to Manage reservation on united.com or in the app.
2. Select your trip and choose Seats.
3. Pick available seats for each traveler and save.

Seat options and any fees depend on your fare (Basic Economy, Economy, Economy Plus® or premium cabins). If you need accessible seating, contact Accessibility Services before travel day.
